name: Rosengartenschlucht
kurzbeschreibung: A spectacular gorge with roaring waterfalls, walkways, and bridges – a unique natural experience right near Imst.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Rosengartenschlucht gorge ranks among the most captivating and geologically significant natural monuments in Tyrol. Emerging directly from the historic town center of Imst, this wildly romantic, deeply incised limestone gorge carves its way over nearly two kilometers up to the alpine hamlet of Hoch-Imst. Over millennia, the tempestuous Schinderbach torrent has sliced through solid rock, fashioning an awe-inspiring labyrinth of thunderous waterfalls, swirling pothole kettles, overhanging rock galleries, and lush emerald moss carpets. Its poetic name ("Rose Garden Gorge") stems from local alpine lore and the delicate pink-blooming alpine flora clinging to protected rock crevices. Near the upper end of the gorge lies the mystical "Blue Grotto" (Blaue Grotte), a historic mining cavern where Roman miners prospected for lead and silver more than two millennia ago.

Route & Requirements

The gorge trek commences in downtown Imst beside the landmark Church of Saint John (Johanneskirche). Extending roughly 1.5 kilometers, the secured trail gains 250 vertical meters (approx. 1.5 hours uphill walking time, moderate grade T2). Hikers traverse cantilevered timber boardwalks, stone steps, hand-hewn rock tunnels, and narrow suspension footbridges directly above the raging glacial torrent. At the upper portal, visitors encounter the atmospheric Blue Grotto, where sunlight filtering through cavern openings casts mesmerizing azure reflections across natural rock pools. From the grotto, a brief walk leads into Hoch-Imst, home to a swimming lake and the Imster Bergbahnen lifts. Walkers can descend via the sunny Wettersteig trail or ride the convenient regional bus back to town. Due to continuous spray, timber planks and rock steps remain damp; sturdy footwear with high-traction lugged soles is strictly mandatory. The gorge is entirely impassable for strollers or wheelchairs due to numerous steps. Leashed, sure-footed dogs are permitted.

Visit & Arrival

Rail travelers arrive at Imst-Pitztal mainline station via frequent ÖBB trains, boarding local city buses (lines 1 or 2) directly to the Imst Stadtplatz or Johanneskirche stop right at the gorge trailhead. Motorists arrive via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Imst) or toll-free across the Fernpass highway B179. Pay and short-term parking is located near the parish church (Pfarrplatz) and the Imst sports arena. The gorge is open daily free of charge from early May through late October (closed in winter due to ice and rockfall hazard).

Tips

Pair your gorge trek with high-speed alpine thrills: hike up through the gorge to Hoch-Imst, take the chairlift to the Untermarkter Alm, and race down on the Alpine Coaster Imst—the longest alpine coaster in the world. The gorge provides natural air-conditioning on scorching summer afternoons.
